standard: Landometer Master Brand Brief v0.5.3 §7.2 (Who / What / Which / How) with the §3.7 evidence standard
dataset_name_th: ฟิตเนสและสตูดิโอในประเทศไทย
category: Location · branch network of a declared brand set
outcome_layer: See → Understand → Decide (act and learn are future extensions)
status: public demo 0.3.0 on GitHub Pages; research master, not a market census

positioning.one_line_highlight: แผนที่เมือง 3 มิติของสาขาฟิตเนสและสตูดิโอในไทย ที่บอกว่ากระจุกตรงไหน เป็นแบบไหน และใครอยู่เบื้องหลัง พร้อมหลักฐานรายสาขา
positioning.unique_advantage: format × district × company in one view, every row linked to the brand’s own official page with its check date and status; districts are CityMETER production codes matched from each row’s own data with the method recorded
positioning.unique_vs_competitors: map search shows points, brand locators one brand at a time, class-booking apps only their partners, company searches no locations — none of them reads format concentration by district with the companies behind the brands and per-row evidence

primary_users: expansion teams of fitness and studio chains
leasing and asset teams of shopping centres, offices and mixed-use projects
analysts, investors and advisors in location and wellness
functional_needs: see where branches of peer brands cluster by district
see whether a district is studio-led or gym-led
see which company operates or invests behind a brand, with evidence
separate listed branches from announced, closed and unclear ones
emotional_needs: not open next to a competitor unknowingly
defend a shortlist with sources and dates
reach the right decision maker of a brand

users.value_proposition: answer where, which format and who in one screen within a minute, every number traceable to an official page
users.evidence: Hypothesis — not yet validated with external users (hypotheses_to_validate)

problem.statement: fitness branch information is scattered across each brand’s locator, social pages and booking apps; none shows which format concentrates in which district and who is behind the brands
problem.urgency: fitness sites tie up long leases and fixed fit-outs (Inference)
problem.severity: a wrong district or format is costly and slow to reverse (Inference)

present_competitors.name: Map search (e.g. Google Maps)
present_competitors.how_users_use_it: search “fitness / pilates near …” and scan the pins
present_competitors.gap: point by point, no district reading, verified brands mixed with any pin, no companies

present_competitors.name: Each brand’s branch locator
present_competitors.how_users_use_it: open brand by brand and copy into a spreadsheet
present_competitors.gap: one brand at a time, different formats, no cross-brand comparison, repeated work

present_competitors.name: Class-booking apps covering many studios
present_competitors.how_users_use_it: see which neighbourhoods have bookable classes
present_competitors.gap: only partner studios, no official status, no companies

present_competitors.name: Company searches
present_competitors.how_users_use_it: look up who holds a brand
present_competitors.gap: not tied to branches or districts; requires knowing the company first

present_competitors.name: Consultant reports and field visits
present_competitors.gap: expensive, slow, quickly outdated, hard to repeat

aspirational_competitors: location intelligence platforms with visit data (depth of demand signal)
competitor_landscape.expected_quality_bar: where / which format / who in one screen within a minute; every figure opens its official source; statuses never mixed; missing never shown as zero

winning_strategy: per-branch evidence from official pages with separated statuses (listed / announced / closed / review)
district reading on CityMETER production codes, matched from each row’s own data with the method recorded and the unplaced counted apart
district personality: studio share of the concentrated districts against the rest of the province, both bases stated
companies behind brands by recorded role with evidence links, and brands recorded with the same company

3D focus scene that opens on the finding, and a building view that turns corner-on to the building, fits it to the free part of the screen and never lets another building hide it — ready for a meeting room
brand first: the brand logo and name before the branch wherever a branch is named (pins, popup, lists, cards, table, brand chart), so a reader recognises the brand before reading
the next question of each view one tap away: Google Search AI Mode with a question written for that view, Google Maps, and Street View where a point exists — results stay Google’s, not CityMETER data
primary_decisions: which district to open next and in which format
which fitness brand to court for a building and whom to contact
which operators and investors matter in a district
primary_questions: สาขาฟิตเนสกระจุกอยู่ตรงไหน และเป็นฟิตเนสแบบไหน
แบรนด์นี้มีบริษัทใดอยู่เบื้องหลัง
ใครกำลังประกาศเปิดสาขา
channel_readiness: demo for conversations with customers, funders and the internal team; not a production dataset
primary_decision_actions: open the official source of a branch
compare districts and brands in the charts
open the same district in CityMETER production
ask Google AI Mode the next question of the view (a branch: open, hours, membership, reviews; a building: which gyms are inside; a district: how they compare; a brand: branches, operator, price)
look at the street in Street View where the view has a point
data_sources: CityMETER Fitness Thailand — Research Master 2026-10-26 (internal sheet; export sha256 in data/fitness.json meta.exportSha256)
CityMETER Shopping Center registry: venues by id from 07_SHOPPING_CENTERS (7) and the public registry snapshot montri-th/shoppingcenter@2eb5532 (2026-10-26) for linked venues the tab does not carry
brand logos: research master 16_BRAND_LOGOS and the research team’s logo library (126 files, SHA-256 checked; data/brand-logos.json); venue logos of the linked venues from the registry snapshot (56)
Google Search AI Mode, Google Maps and Street View — outbound links only; nothing is read back into the data
CityMETER production base info and boundaries (receipts in data/boundary-receipts.json)
OpenGISData-Thailand names (CC BY 4.0) for reading English addresses
spatial_granularity: เขต/อำเภอ (282 of 352 listed branches); province (40); none (30); points on 157 rows (28 source points, 129 venue reference points)
temporal_coverage: single check of each official page on 2026-10-26
update_frequency: per research round; no automatic refresh yet (backlog N03)
key_metrics: branches per เขต/อำเภอ (count)
share of the leading province’s placed branches in the focused districts
studio share (focus vs rest of the province)
visual_layers: brand logo chips beside the brand name on HTML pins at detail zoom (as many as fit without overlap, the selected and nearest the centre first), popups, lists, cards, table and the brand chart
district choropleth (LDS count, all 41 samples by rank)
format cue symbols for rows with a point
OSM massing (focus tier rounded, city tier quiet; see-through in front of the building being looked at)
the building being looked at in the data colour, drawn over every other building and road name (x-ray)

unit.row: one row of 02_STORES — a source-qualified branch observation (official operator page, locator, social profile or announcement); not a field-verified storefront
unit.default: listed — rows whose source still lists the service on the check date (source_listed); announced, closed and review rows are counted apart and never added to it

adminMethods.point: published source point inside the production district (display outline; points within 150 m of an edge confirmed on full-resolution production subdistrict geometry)
adminMethods.host: CityMETER Shopping Center id → registry reference point (07_SHOPPING_CENTERS) → production district
adminMethods.address: the row's own address text (scripts/admin_text.py): marker · pair · mueang · trailing
adminMethods.province: province only (the sheet's province, else the province or single-province postcode the address states)
adminMethods.conflict: the sheet's province disagrees with the row's own address or point — placed nowhere, listed in meta.conflicts
adminMethods.none: no province anywhere in the row

conflicts.note: address points to สมุทรปราการ

excludedFields: sister_brand_names (15_SISTER_BRANDS: Thai presence mostly not established)
data_transparency.provenanceLine: every panel view ends with dataset · source · date · boundary and what one counted unit is

known_limitations: a declared set of 126 brands, not every fitness business in Thailand
70 of 352 listed branches have no district (province only, no province, or a province conflict)
157 rows have a point, 129 of them a venue’s registry reference point (not a shopfront); pins are not the distribution — district colours are
status = what the official page shows on the check date, not daily opening, size, members, price or footfall
company names as the sources state them, not checked against the company registry; a missing record does not mean independent

147 rows are linked to 128 CityMETER venues by id (13 of them without a registry reference point yet); 19 rows are held candidates (name or numbering, registry duplicate, parent component) and are never drawn as links; the links were written into the research sheet on 2026-10-30 and read back cell by cell — the demo never links by name

one list per building merges venue-linked rows and rows whose own points fall in the building (display-time join on the footprints the map draws); one unlinked own point sits 22 m from a venue point (Gateway Ekamai)
building footprints and heights are OpenStreetMap context via OpenFreeMap; the building view frames what the tiles draw

logos identify the brand next to its name and are not a trademark licence; 62 of 126 are the original bytes, the rest a recorded uniform downscale, transparent-margin trim or SVG namespace fix (both SHA-256 kept); 3 (The Cult Fitness Society, Red Rock Canyon Climbing Gym, Fitness7) sit on a dark chip because the library’s recommended light surface hides their white artwork (recorded in data/brand-logos.json surfaceNote, reported to the research team)

Google AI Mode, Maps and Street View open outside the demo; their answers are Google’s and may disagree with the official pages; Street View near a venue uses the registry reference point, not the shop entrance
data-use rights of each source not yet reviewed (backlog N02)
example_use_cases: a studio founder shortlists districts where studios are not yet dense
a leasing team lists gym brands absent from its district and the companies to approach
an analyst maps operators and investors behind the largest brands

hypotheses_to_validate.hypothesis: H1 expansion teams answer “which district next and why” from the first screen within a minute
hypotheses_to_validate.test: 5 real users on their own task, timed and asked to explain
hypotheses_to_validate.criterion: ≥ 4/5 answer with a figure and its source within 60 s

hypotheses_to_validate.hypothesis: H2 the studio share changes how specialist studios shortlist districts
hypotheses_to_validate.test: interview 3–5 studio founders on real district screens
hypotheses_to_validate.criterion: ≥ 3 say they would use it to shortlist or ask for it elsewhere

hypotheses_to_validate.hypothesis: H3 the companies behind brands are valuable enough for leasing teams to reuse
hypotheses_to_validate.test: 3 leasing teams prepare a contact list with the brand cards
hypotheses_to_validate.criterion: ≥ 2 reuse it within two weeks or ask for more brands

hypotheses_to_validate.hypothesis: H4 stating the unplaced branches raises trust rather than confusion
hypotheses_to_validate.test: A/B the line under the first finding with 6 users

hypotheses_to_validate.hypothesis: H5 a quarterly refresh is enough for location decisions
hypotheses_to_validate.criterion: < 10% of branches change status per quarter, else refresh more often
